facts.text: Fox Crossing is located at the north end of Lake Winnebago along the Fox River, which forms Little Lake Butte des Morts.
European immigrants settled the area now known as Fox Crossing in the 1830s following treaties with the Menominee tribe.
Fox Crossing was incorporated in 2016 from the former town of Menasha to secure greater local authority over planning and zoning.
The region faces seasonal flooding risks from the Fox River, which has a history of overflowing during heavy rains and spring thaws.
Fox Crossing experiences a humid continental climate, characterized by cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers.
Early history in Fox Crossing was marked by border struggles and legal disputes with the neighboring towns of Clayton and Neenah.
